summary: Frontend-only regression to confirm the React crash 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {type, loc, msg, input, ctx})' is fixed by the new errMessage() helper. Forced real server 422s through the UI using Playwright request interception (mutating the outgoing POST /api/bookings and PATCH /api/admin/bookings/{job} bodies) so the actual axios error path in the app was exercised. All 7 checks passed: (1) 422 on booking submit renders a readable toast 'customer_phone: String should have at least 10 characters, preferred_time: Field required' with no React crash and no error overlay, user stays on the form; (2) valid booking submit succeeds and lands on /book/success with job number KHR-2026-000005; (3) /track with 'KHR-INVALID' shows friendly string 'Request not found' in [data-testid=track-error]; (4) /admin/login with wrong password shows toast 'Invalid email or password'; (5) valid admin login reaches /admin dashboard; (6) forced 422 on admin PATCH shows 'estimated_cost: Input should be a valid number, unable to parse string as a number' with zero pageerrors; (7) valid admin PATCH shows 'Updated' toast and persists (audit history entry added). No pageerror events and no [object Object] leakage anywhere. Backend re-verified implicitly: POST /api/bookings returned 200 for a valid payload.

critical_code_review_comments: errMessage() is correct but falls back to err.message before the supplied fallback, so a network failure surfaces raw axios text like 'Network Error'/'Request failed with status code 500' to end users. Consider only using err.message for non-HTTP (no response) errors, and using the human fallback whenever err.response exists.
BookingPage.jsx onUpload() aborts the whole loop on the first failed upload and still shows a single generic toast - per-file error reporting would be clearer, but not a blocker.

rca_of_the_issue: FastAPI returns 422 with detail as a list of pydantic error dicts. Previously that list was passed straight into toast.error()/setErr(), so React tried to render an object and threw. The fix (errMessage in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js) flattens the array into 'loc: msg' strings joined by commas, stringifies plain-object details, and falls back to err.message/fallback - verified to always return a string in both the array-detail (422) and string-detail (401/404) cases.
